highlightAliases.new: Late-onset AD accounts for more than 95% of cases in the chapter's estimate (p894). Familial AD accounts for 1–5% and is one cause of younger-onset AD. Younger-onset disease can also occur without a causative familial mutation (p897).

highlightAliases.old: Aducanumab — FDA accelerated approval June 2021 (p911); anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody, FDA-labeled only for MCI due to AD and mild AD (not moderate-to-severe AD) (Table 59-7, p914). highlightAliases.new: Aducanumab received FDA accelerated approval in June 2021 after trials in MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia (p911, Table 59-7, p914). EMERGE found 22% less worsening on CDR-SB over 18 months. ENGAGE did not show significant benefit. In the pooled 10 mg/kg groups, 35.2% had ARIA-E, 41.3% had any ARIA-E or ARIA-H, and 75.8% of participants with any ARIA were asymptomatic (EMERGE/ENGAGE safety analysis, Tables 1 and 3).

highlightAliases.new: Of 1,029 high-dose participants, 425 (41.3%) had ARIA-E or ARIA-H, including 362 (35.2%) with ARIA-E. Among the 425 with any ARIA, 103 (24.2%) had symptoms and 322 (75.8%) did not (p911, EMERGE/ENGAGE integrated safety analysis, Tables 1 and 3).
